# L-29304 — Transition-band positive normal form (research)

Status: PROPOSED RESEARCH LEMMA — NOT PROVED

The first-entrance decomposition suggests that the remaining obstruction should be expressed in a finite transition band rather than in the full ancestry tree.

For the size-biased fragmentation kernel Q, define Sigma_{X,n} on [n,2n) by first entrance below 2n. Any two realizations with the same Sigma differ by a divergence-free balanced flow.

The proposed normal form is:

Sigma_{X,n}=C_{X,n}+S_{X,n}+P_{X,n}+R_{X,n}

where:

* C is generated by Pascal four-cycles and has zero divergence;
* S consists of squarefree collector generators with zero proper-power leakage;
* P consists of parity/factor-five boundary generators;
* R is coordinatewise nonnegative.

If this decomposition can be constructed with finite nonnegative coefficients, then the original producer positivity follows without requiring Sigma itself to be positive coordinatewise.

The new production target is therefore not GFEP directly but a constructive transition-band normal form algorithm.

Required certificate:

1. exact first-entrance ledger;
2. cycle coordinates;
3. squarefree collector coordinates;
4. parity boundary coordinates;
5. residual positivity certificate.

No asymptotic sign claim is made here.
